title: Greet with better
hook: when greeted, return a better greeting or the same (4:86)

segments.voice: Yesterday: in a dispute, refer it back to God and the messenger, a source above both sides. Your line was refer it back. Did you name a shared principle before making your case? Day three hundred eighty-four.

Someone texts you: good morning! And you reply: morning. Someone at work says: hope your weekend was great. You say: yep, you too. Nothing wrong with it. But you've probably felt the difference when someone answers you with a little more than you gave: a name, a question, a real wish. It lands. An-Nisa, between laws about war and peace, stops to give a rule about something as small as hello.
screen: `GOOD MORNING! → MORNING.` → `A LITTLE MORE THAN YOU GAVE.` → `A RULE ABOUT HELLO.`

segments.voice: Here's 4:86 in Pickthall's words: "When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it. Lo! Allah taketh count of all things." The word for greeting is tahiyyah, from the root of hayah, life: a greeting, at its root, is a wish for someone's life. The rule has two levels. The minimum: give back what you were given. The better way: add to it. The Muslim greeting shows how. As-salamu 'alaykum: peace be upon you. The better reply adds a layer: wa 'alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullah, and upon you be peace, and God's mercy. Better still: wa barakatuh, and His blessings. There's a hadith in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi about exactly this. A man came and said as-salamu 'alaykum, and the Prophet ﷺ answered him and said: ten. Another came and added wa rahmatullah; twenty. A third added wa barakatuh; thirty. Ten good deeds for each piece. And a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari takes the custom back to the beginning. When God created Adam, He told him to go and greet a group of angels and listen to their answer, because it would be the greeting of his children. Adam said as-salamu 'alaykum. The angels replied: as-salamu 'alayka wa rahmatullah. They added mercy. The very first greeting, answered with better. And notice the verse's last line. God takes count of all things, even a hello. Nothing kind is too small to be noticed.
screen: `TAHIYYAH: A WISH FOR LIFE` · `RETURN IT, OR BETTER` · `TEN, TWENTY, THIRTY` · `THE ANGELS ADDED MERCY` · then, large: `GREET YE WITH A BETTER THAN IT.`

segments.voice: When the bell starts, think of the last few greetings you received: a text, a hello at the door, a message from a coworker. Remember how you answered. Now picture answering each one again, a little better. Use their name. Add a real wish: I hope your mother's feeling better. Have a good day at the new job. If you greet with salam, add the mercy and the blessings. Choose the next person you'll greet with better. The bell holds the time.
Greet with better. When greeted, return a better greeting, or at least the same, from 4:86; God takes count of all things. Today's word.
Your line: greet with better. Today, answer every greeting with a little more than you were given: a name, a wish, a smile. Day three hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims greet each other with as-salamu 'alaykum and are taught to return it with at least the same, and ideally more: wa 'alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
